ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, every proposed director, shareholder, beneficial owner, authorized representative and bank account signatory must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Hong Kong Monetary Authority AML/CFT sanction notices, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and PRC sanctions and unreliable entity lists. Each person must be assessed for politically exposed person status, family members and close associates using a written CDD file verifying identity, source of wealth, source of funds and country risk. Any sanctions hit requires immediate suspension and a suspicious transaction report to the HK Financial Intelligence Unit under Cap. 615; PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry / Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) name search facility
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Hong Kong company name may be in English, Chinese, or both; a Chinese name must consist solely of Chinese characters, and the English and Chinese names need not be direct translations. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) the mandatory 'Limited' indicator; (2) a distinctive trade-markable element; (3) a permissible descriptive business descriptor such as 'Gaming Technology' or 'Anti-Cheat Software'; and (4) absence of prohibited, confusing, criminal or government-implying terms. For mainland WFOE documents, the approved Chinese name must be transliterated into English by standardized Hanyu Pinyin whenever a cross-border registration requires a romanized name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Hong Kong Companies Registry refuses a proposed name, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar within 21 days from the rejection notice, setting out the registry search reference, the disputed name, the grounds of distinctiveness, and any letter of consent from the relevant statutory authority; the Registrar must issue a written determination. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may apply for leave to commence judicial review in the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. For a mainland WFOE parent, a rejected Chinese name is contestable by administrative reconsideration to the next higher SAMR authority within 60 days and thereafter by administrative litigation in the competent People's Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) because a physical Hong Kong address is required for service of process and statutory notices. For the video-game kernel-level anti-cheat and integrity middleware industry, the Inland Revenue Department and particular banks will expect substantive commercial substance: a physical office with employees or binding subcontract arrangements, audit records, service contracts, and source-code or hardware documentation. A virtual office may be used only as auxiliary mail forwarding and cannot satisfy HKMA CDD expectations for opening a bank account with Swift/Wire and Stripe payment-rail capability; the mainland WFOE parent must also maintain its own physical registered premises under SAMR rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered office signage and accessibility during business hours; (2) statutory records and board minutes kept at the registered office; (3) original bank statements, tax returns, invoices and payroll records available on site; (4) employees or authorized agents present; (5) software licensing/service agreements evidencing the anti-cheat engine business; (6) employer returns matched to payroll; (7) audited financial statements available. Quantified risk: for this Hong Kong-incorporated entity with no public-facing office, the Inland Revenue Department field-audit or physical-inspection probability is estimated at 12-18% within the first two financial years; Companies Registry inspections are rare but may follow complaints; the mainland WFOE parent carries a SAMR random-inspection probability of approximately 10-15% annually if it is selected for the municipal double-random inspection scheme.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, as amended, together with the Companies (Fees and Dues) Regulation and the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), including the provisions governing company incorporation by registration, Articles of Association, registered office, directors, company secretary, share capital allotment and statutory registers; and the Business Registration Ordinance section concerning mandatory business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department as the connected authority for business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NNC1 (Incorporation of a Company Limited by Shares) together with the Articles of Association, director and company secretary consent forms, and the prescribed filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong SAR imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a private company limited by shares. The incorporators may state any nominal issued share capital, commonly HK$1.00; there is no blocked escrow account, paid-up capital deposit, bank capital verification or Companies Registry capital control requirement. Any bank or counterparty may independently impose a higher commercial capital or net asset condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a duly convened first meeting of the Board of Directors of CN JV Limited (the Company) held at the registered office located at [Registered Office Address], Hong Kong SAR, on [Date], due notice having been waived by all directors, and all directors being present, the chairman stated that the meeting was validly constituted and that a quorum was in attendance. The following resolutions were submitted and passed unanimously by the first board. (1) RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Ordinance Cap. 622, with the English name CN JV Limited and such additional names as the registrar has approved, is ratified, accepted and confirmed in all respects. (2) RESOLVED that the subscription, allotment and issue of the initial share capital of 10,000 ordinary shares of HK$1.00 each, fully paid in cash, is hereby ratified, approved and confirmed, and that the directors are authorized to accept subscriptions and financial contributions from the Sino-Foreign joint venture shareholders and to allot further shares on such terms as the board considers necessary for the gaming anti-cheat engine business, provided that all allotments comply with the Companies Ordinance and the Articles of Association. (3) RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Registered Office Address], Hong Kong SAR, and that the company secretary is directed to maintain there the register of members, register of directors, register of secretaries, minutes and other statutory records, and to notify the Companies Registry of any future change using the prescribed form. (4) RESOLVED that the statutory corporate officers are appointed as follows: [Name] as Director and Principal Executive Officer, [Name] as Director, [Name] as Non-Executive Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Auditor, each to serve according to the Articles of Association and until removed or reappointed. (5) RESOLVED that the directors and account signatories designated in the banking mandate are authorized to open, operate, maintain and close bank, merchant, SWIFT wire and Stripe settlement accounts in the name of the Company with licensed financial institutions, to execute account application documents, treasury forms and indemnities, to sign checks and payment orders, to transfer funds, to borrow money up to the limit separately approved by the board, and to delegate routine treasury operations to the Company's finance officer within limits set by the board. This resolution shall remain in full force until superseded by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Corporate Name Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Cyber Search Centre and Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the ICRIS Cyber Search Centre to search the Companies Registry index for existing company names, business registration names and statutory bodies. The selected English name must end with Limited; the Chinese name, if used, must be composed of permitted characters and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name. Confirm that the proposed CN JV Limited name is not prohibited by regulations and does not infringe a known trademark. Record the search output in the incorporation dossier and submit the name with Form NNC1; if any shareholder approval is required under the joint venture agreement, obtain the written consent of the joint venture parties before filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed English company name
Proposed Chinese company name if desired
ICRIS name search report and extracts
Written authorization from proposed directors and shareholders to use the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry rejects the proposed name or a third party objects, the company secretary must select an alternative name and file an amended Form NNC1; if the conflict is based on similarity, the adverse action may be cured by a letter of consent from the objecting entity or by a Registrar direction, and prompt refiling avoids additional objector costs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, e-Registry online filing portal or registered company formation branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the incorporation package after legal and commercial due diligence. Complete Form NNC1 in English or Chinese setting out the proposed name, registered office address, directors, company secretary, shareholders, share class, and issued share capital. Obtain signed consent from each first director and each first company secretary. The Articles of Association must be printed, paginated, and executed by each subscriber in the presence of a witness when required by registry practice or by the opening bank. Submit the package through the Companies Registry e-Registry portal or at the counter, pay the applicable fees, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation. Preserve a duplicate set of certified documents in the joint venture corporate records.
required_dossiers: Fully completed and signed Form NNC1
Articles of Association executed by all subscribers
Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
Signed consent to act as company secretary for the proposed secretary
Copy of each director and subscriber passport or Hong Kong identity card
Proof of the proposed registered office address in Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a query or suspends the application, submit a legal cover letter, a statutory declaration and any missing consent forms within 14 calendar days; if the defect is an incomplete form, file a corrected NNC1; a refusal on name grounds is remedied by filing a fresh incorporation application with an approved name before paying any additional fee beyond the non-refundable search charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Inland Revenue Tax File Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation, deliver the Certificate of Incorporation and the completed business registration application to the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department. The application must state the principal business activity as computer programming and software middleware for gaming security under ISIC 6201, the place of business in Hong Kong, the expected commencement date, and contact details. Pay the annual business registration fee and statutory levy. Upon issue, verify that the Business Registration Certificate states the correct company name, business code and address, and arrange display of the certificate at the principal place of business as required by law.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Companies Registry
Completed Business Registration application form
Copy of Form NNC1 as filed
Copy of registered office address proof such as lease or landlord consent
Photocopies of director identification documents
Business commencement date and short business plan for the anti-cheat middleware activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Officer queries the place of business or revenue estimate, provide the lease or a solicitor's confirmation and a detailed business model letter; if the certificate is issued with an incorrect company name or ISIC code, file a written correction request within seven days; late application may attract penalties, and the company may seek the IRD's written remission if the delay was caused by the registry or postal service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption and Banking Authorization Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry for registered office records and licensed bank or authorized payment institution under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution ratified in this dossier. Ratify the issue of shares, adopt the registered office, appoint statutory officers, and approve the banking mandate. Using these resolutions, complete the know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering forms for each director and beneficial owner, provide source of funds documentation, a corporate structure chart, and a Companies Registry record to open a corporate bank account with a licensed bank or a licensed stored value facility. Maintain all banking records and ensure joint signatures are materially consistent with the board resolution. The registered office must remain a physical Hong Kong address open during ordinary office hours, and any relocation must be notified to the Companies Registry by Form NR1.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the first board resolutions
Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Articles of Association of CN JV Limited
Identification and proof of address for each authorized signatory and beneficial owner
Corporate structure chart showing the Sino-Foreign joint venture ownership
Banking mandate together with source of funds and business plan
Compliance declaration regarding PEP or known source of wealth where relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank imposes enhanced due diligence or refuses the application, supply a legal opinion on the corporate structure and beneficial ownership, audited or management financial statements, and a refined source of funds narrative; alternatively present the mandate to another HKMA-licensed bank or authorized payment institution; any change of signatories requires a supplemental board resolution and updated bank forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Compliance and Licensing Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, Environmental Protection Department and Fire Services Department as applicable; for this digital scope, licensing is Not Applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Implement post-incorporation governance by maintaining the statutory registers of members, directors, company secretary, charges and debentures at the registered office; notify the Companies Registry of any allotment or charge using the prescribed returns; issue share certificates; and confirm that the company secretary and auditor hold office in accordance with the Ordinance. For ISIC 6201 pure digital software and anti-cheat middleware, prepare a written internal compliance memorandum stating that no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity exists, and therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment designation, Civil Defense fire permit or industrial operating license is required. If the company later leases physical office premises, obtain the landlord's fire safety certificate and ensure compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance before staff occupy the site.
required_dossiers: Statutory registers of members, directors and company secretary
Allotment return and share certificate records
First board meeting minutes and officer consents
Auditor consent and company secretary consent
Office lease and landlord fire safety certificate if physical premises are occupied
Internal memorandum confirming EIA and fire permit non-application for digital software activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a post-incorporation return is rejected or filed late, submit the corrected or late form with the prescribed late fee and request an administrative no-prosecution letter from the Companies Registry if the delay was inadvertent; if the Environmental Protection Department nevertheless raises an inquiry because of cloud hosting or colocation, provide the hosting provider's environmental permits and a legal opinion confirming that the Company has no operational control of physical data center equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. CN JV Limited is engaged in ISIC 6201 computer programming and gaming anti-cheat middleware software development; it is not engaged in physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing in Hong Kong SAR.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. Under Hong Kong SAR law, no industrial operating license, factory concession, or sectoral manufacturing permit is required for pure digital software and middleware distribution; the relevant compliance obligations are corporate registration, business registration, payroll tax, and any contractual software export controls.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable. Pure software engineering for kernel-level anti-cheat middleware does not constitute a designated project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499), Schedule 2; no EIA report, no environmental permit, and no statutory environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The activity produces no wastewater discharge, no VOC emissions, no atmospheric stack emissions and no hazardous waste streams. Cloud infrastructure and server hosting, if used, are operated by licensed third-party data center providers, and the Company should rely on those providers' environmental permits and ISO 14001 certifications in its procurement records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No civil defense fire permit under the Fire Safety (Buildings) Ordinance (Cap. 502), no dangerous goods license, and no structural load inspection is required for a non-manufacturing software company. For any leased office premises, the landlord must supply a valid fire services certificate, emergency lighting and means of escape certificates, and the Company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) for workstation ergonomics, electrical safety and emergency procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China (electronic tax portal www.chinatax.gov.cn and e-Tax China); Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (electronic portal www.ird.gov.hk)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture in Mainland China: (1) Execute the joint venture contract and articles of association; (2) Submit incorporation registration to the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the SAMR e-registration system and receive the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which operates as the sole corporate statutory identifier and is automatically accepted by the STA as the PRC tax identification number; (3) Complete tax registration through the e-Tax portal within 30 days of SAMR issuance; the USCC is confirmed as the taxpayer identification number for corporate income tax and VAT; (4) For the foreign non-resident shareholder without a permanent establishment, the JV performs withholding tax remittance using the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction TIN and, if treaty relief is claimed, files the requisite Tax Residency Certificate with the STA; (5) If a Hong Kong vehicle or branch is also employed, apply to the IRD Business Registration Office for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance and obtain a Companies Registry company number; the Hong Kong Business Registration Number serves as the Hong Kong taxpayer identification. All foreign charter documents must be notarized and, where applicable, apostilled; a locally appointed joint venture legal representative or authorized tax agent must execute the registration filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the CN_JV_LTD is a PRC resident enterprise liable to Corporate Income Tax on worldwide income; in the Hong Kong nexus, any separately incorporated HK entity branch or offshore-profits claim is subject to entity-level profits tax on a territorial-source basis with no pass-through treatment; the gaming anti-cheat middleware is ordinary software and technology service activity and does not fall into any tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Neither the PRC nor Hong Kong tax system provides check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections for a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture; entity classification is mandatory under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Ordinance. Available administrative elections are limited to VAT general versus small-scale taxpayer status within statutory thresholds, depreciation methods, and treaty benefit claims, none of which alter entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) in Mainland China; Hong Kong SAR has no general VAT, GST or sales tax, though stamp duty, customs duties and a small set of excise duties may apply
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PRC: all entities must tax-register upon establishment; there is no monetary turnover threshold for VAT registration. Mandatory conversion to general VAT taxpayer status applies when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000, while annual taxable sales at or below CNY 5,000,000 may remain small-scale taxpayer status. HK: no VAT/GST registration threshold exists because no such tax is imposed; only Business Registration under the Business Registration Ordinance is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mainland China operates a real-time fiscal electronic invoice infrastructure through the STA e-Tax platform. General VAT invoices and Special VAT invoices are issued through the VAT invoice control system, with invoice data transmitted to the STA in near real time. Full Digital Electronic Invoices are generated on the e-Tax system and carry a unique QR code and encrypted electronic seal, eliminating the need for a physical fiscal stamp. High-volume taxpayers may use STA-approved APIs for automated machine-to-machine invoice issuance and reporting. Hong Kong does not mandate an electronic invoicing clearance system or real-time fiscal stamping; ordinary commercial invoices and receipts governed by IRD record-keeping rules are acceptable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under PRC VAT law and the Ministry of Finance/STA measures on cross-border taxable services, export sales of goods are zero-rated, and qualifying cross-border taxable services, including software middleware licensing, technical support and anti-cheat engine deployment supplied to non-resident recipients, are zero-rated or exempted provided the recipient is located outside Mainland China, the service is wholly consumed outside Mainland China, the consideration is received in foreign exchange, and the exporter files the cross-border service zero-rating declaration on the STA electronic platform. For physical exports, the Customs export declaration and foreign exchange collection verification must be completed. Hong Kong does not impose VAT/GST and therefore no zero-rating is claimed; under the territorial source principle, profits from exports are not subject to Hong Kong profits tax if the goods are sold or services are rendered and the contract was negotiated and concluded outside or ex-Hong Kong, supported by the full transactional trail.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration Form issued by the Customs of the People's Republic of China for physical exports or for software delivered on physical media
Export Bill of Lading or Master Air Waybill evidencing the movement of goods out of Mainland China
Cross-Border Taxable Service Export Contract or Software Licensing Agreement executed with the overseas customer

Digital delivery evidence for anti-cheat middleware, including activation keys, licensing server logs, API access timestamps, or server-side download records demonstrating overseas consumption outside Mainland China

Report on Receipt of Foreign Exchange under the integrated State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) system showing foreign currency received and repatriated to the PRC exporting entity's bank account
Full Digital Electronic Invoice or Special VAT Invoice issued through the STA platform for the zero-rated export transaction
Acknowledgment or filing record of the cross-border taxable service zero-rating declaration accepted by the STA electronic portal
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, SAFE and Customs may jointly audit export zero-rating claims. If the zero-rating is unsupported or documentation is deficient, the exported transaction is recharacterized as domestic taxable supply, the VAT at the applicable rate is clawed back with statutory late payment interest, and administrative penalties from 0.5 to 5 times the underpaid tax may be imposed for fraudulent or negligent zero-rating. Criminal liability for tax evasion and smuggling penalties can arise in serious cases. In Hong Kong, inaccurate territorial-source assertions are reassessed by the IRD; onshore profits are charged at the prevailing profits tax rate of 16.5% for corporations, with the two-tier rate of 8.25% applied to the first HK$2 million assessable profits, plus interest and potential penalties up to three times the tax undercharged. Retrospective assessments are available under applicable limitation periods, with no limitation for fraudulent concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC), acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), for mainland China; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the linked-rate central banking authority for Hong Kong SAR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under mainland China's FX framework, the RMB is convertible on the current account for genuine trade and services transactions, but the capital account is heavily administered by SAFE. The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture (CN_JV_LTD) must open a SAFE-registered FDI capital account for inbound equity subscriptions; RMB converted from foreign-exchange capital can be deployed only within the approved business scope and cannot be used for equity investment, securities, wealth-management products, or unauthorized on-lending. Current-account export proceeds are subject to repatriation into China but no longer to a fixed mandatory surrender ratio; the JV may retain FX in a designated settlement account or convert it to RMB at a domestic Tier-1 bank. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permitted but requires audited financial statements, corporate income tax clearance, a board-approved dividend resolution, and SAFE transaction reporting; dividend withholding tax applies. Hong Kong SAR has a fully convertible HKD, no foreign-exchange controls, no surrender rules, and no profit-remittance approvals, making it the natural treasury conduit. Every cross-border flow between the mainland JV and the HK treasury vehicle must nevertheless cross the PBoC/SAFE barrier using correct BOP purpose codes, underlying contracts, and bank verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For mainland China, export proceeds from the JV's software and middleware sales must be repatriated into a domestic foreign-exchange settlement account or RMB account at a designated bank by the contractual payment due date; if the contract contains no due date, the bank applies a practical 90-day collection benchmark from the invoice or services-completion date, and receipts beyond that window require deferred-receivables registration or a supplementary SAFE explanation. There is no fixed statutory percentage of export receipts that must be converted into RMB; the JV may retain all collected FX or convert at its own discretion. For Hong Kong, there is no surrender requirement and no conversion mandate for HKD or any foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account for current-account receipts
Multi-currency Corporate Treasury Account (HKD/CNY/USD) for the HK treasury vehicle with CHATS and CIPS access

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Settlement Account (Capital Account) for inbound equity subscriptions and SAFE-backed capital conversion
Export proceeds verification and sweep account for cross-border SaaS and anti-cheat licensing income

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is LOW as a primary treasury rail for the mainland JV, but MEDIUM-HIGH as an ancillary collection and payout channel for the Hong Kong treasury entity. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Airwallex, Neat, Statrys, and Payhawk are not licensed Chinese commercial banks and are legally barred from opening the RMB basic deposit account, the FDI capital settlement account, or the foreign-exchange settlement account that PBoC/SAFE requires the mainland JV to maintain. They also cannot perform export-proceeds repatriation, capital verification, dividend tax clearance, or BOP purpose-code reporting. For the HK entity, a HKMA-authorized bank or licensed EMI may support multi-currency collections, Stripe payouts, and low-value operational cards, but all balances must be swept to the tier-1 bank account at least daily to ensure final clearing in CHATS/CIPS. The EMI must never be used for SAFE-regulated capital-account transactions involving the mainland JV.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mainland China: physical presence is mandatory. The legal representative or the board-appointed authorized signatory must attend the bank branch in person to open the RMB basic account and the FDI capital settlement account; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted. The original business license, company seal, approved JV contract, SAFE foreign-investment registration, and directors' identification documents must be presented. A second signatory may be onboarded through video KYC at some banks, but the primary legal representative must appear in branch. Hong Kong SAR: HKMA permits non-face-to-face onboarding, but most tier-1 banks require an in-person or video interview with at least one director and the confirming UBO. Foreign directors may present a notarized power of attorney and certified passport copy plus a live video call; some HK banks accept remote consular proxy opening for a low-risk entity, but the bank's compliance committee retains discretion. For this structure, we recommend physical attendance for both the mainland JV and the HK treasury vehicle to avoid underwriting delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and control chain spanning mainland China and Hong Kong with multiple-vehicle ownership creating opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full group organizational chart; certified certificate of incorporation from the HK Companies Registry; the Chinese business license and JV approval/filing; a UBO schedule naming every individual with economic interest above 10%; the shareholders register; the JV contract; board minutes appointing all signatories; notarized passports of all UBOs; and a signed declaration confirming no bearer shares, nominee structures, or undisclosed trusts are used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance mismatch where the HK treasury company may appear to be a shell while the mainland JV earns all operating revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a Hong Kong economic substance file containing a lease agreement with utility invoices; payroll, MPF contributions and employment contracts for resident directors and staff; board and shareholder minutes held in Hong Kong; the latest Hong Kong profits tax return and audited financial statements of the HK entity; an arm's-length transfer pricing policy for the royalty or service fee paid by the mainland JV; and the underlying client software licensing agreements naming the HK entity as contracting party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for inbound equity capital injection appears unexplained or is layered through third-party accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds pack: 12 months of bank statements from the remitting shareholder; audited financial statements and corporate income tax filings of the investor; the board resolution or dividend minutes supporting the capital call; the JV capital contribution schedule; notarized evidence of asset disposals if used; tax clearance certificates for any funded profit distributions; and a formal board letter confirming all injected funds are legitimate and free from sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gaming-related terminology creates perceived exposure to unlicensed gambling or casino risk despite ISIC 6201 classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a business scope certificate and customer agreements showing kernel-level anti-cheat middleware, not gambling operations; a compliance attestation that no product is offered in jurisdictions where real-money gaming is unlawful; a whitelist of named game-publisher clients with audited financials; IP and software registration certificates; a negative covenant restricting use for gambling, cheating or rootkit evasion; and statutory confirmation that no gaming operator licence is required under applicable law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing is: (1) the HK treasury vehicle adopts a board resolution approving the capital call and executes the capital contribution schedule in the JV contract; (2) the mainland JV completes the SAFE foreign-invested enterprise registration with the municipal SAFE office or the designated bank, obtaining the FDI registration reference and opening the FDI capital settlement account at a domestic Tier-1 bank; (3) the foreign shareholder remits from its own account in Hong Kong through SWIFT MT103 to the JV's FDI capital settlement account, quoting the SAFE FDI registration number and BOP receipt purpose code 622011 (Inbound Direct Investment - New Establishment) or the bank-mapped current SAFE code; (4) the receiving bank credits the capital account, performs BOP reporting, and verifies the contribution under the JV contract; (5) the JV converts the FX to RMB into an RMB capital settlement account, and each subsequent disbursement requires supporting contracts, invoices and a payment application confirming use within the approved business scope; (6) a Chinese CPA issues the capital verification report if required by the bank or articles, and the registered capital is recorded in the national credit information system. Proceeds must not be used for equity investment, wealth management, unrelated lending, or repayment of offshore debt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For treasury disbursements, the HK treasury vehicle pays global vendors and mainland suppliers using SWIFT MT103 wires with underlying contract and invoice references. For RMB payments to mainland counterparties, the preferred rail is CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) through a clearing bank in Hong Kong, or HKD/USD settlement through the HKMA CHATS system with T+0 finality. For large hardware or engine-

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the company's incorporation anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees apply: HKD 1,260 for delivery made more than 42 days but not more than 3 months late; HKD 2,520 for more than 3 months but not more than 6 months late; HKD 3,780 for more than 6 months late. Non-compliance is an offence and may attract a default fine of up to HKD 50,000. Repeated or persistent non-delivery can lead to prosecution and, where the company lacks business or assets, administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Companies Registry under the Companies Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal and Payment of Business Registration Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry of the current Business Registration Certificate; the renewal demand is normally issued by the IRD one month before the expiry date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew the certificate on time is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance. The IRD may impose late payment penalties, additional fee recovery, and prosecution, with fines and sanctions that can ultimately support deregistration proceedings where the company continues to operate without valid registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) accompanied by audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the issue date of the return; where a tax representative is appointed, the IRD normally grants an extension aligned with the accounting period year-end, commonly extending the filing deadline to several months after issue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger estimated assessments at higher notional profits, a default penalty of up to HKD 10,000, and additional tax of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged. Critical and persistent non-compliance may lead to court summons, criminal conviction, and reinforced deregistration measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A) together with employee tax return schedules where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the issue date of the return; the IRD normally issues the return around 1 April with a due date of 1 May for most taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unreasonable or late failure to file may incur penalties of up to HKD 10,000 per offense; where underassessment is caused, additional tax up to three times the undercharged amount may be assessed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No balance-sheet, turnover, headcount, or size-based audit threshold applies in Hong Kong. Every company incorporated in Hong Kong with legal personality must appoint a certified public accountant and have its financial statements audited, except only where the company qualifies as dormant under section 405 of the Companies Ordinance, Cap.622. Therefore, even a small private company, shell entity, or single-purpose JV company remains subject to the statutory audit requirement if it has any active transaction or does not satisfy the dormancy exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), HKFRS for Private Entities, or the HK SME Financial Reporting Standard as applicable. Full HKFRS, which is substantially converged with IFRS, applies to public-interest entities, listed issuers, banks, insurers, and companies that do not qualify as small private companies; qualifying small private companies may elect HKFRS for Private Entities or HK SME Financial Reporting Standard.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require a public UBO return to the Companies Registry. Instead, every private company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) at its registered office or other prescribed place in Hong Kong, identifying individuals with significant control, including holdings greater than 25% of shares or voting rights, board appointment rights, rights to distributions, or the ability to exercise significant influence or control. The SCR is not open to public inspection but must be produced on demand to authorized enforcement officers. Changes in shareholding or significant control must be recorded in the SCR as soon as practicable and in any event within 7 days of notice; share transfer instruments must be presented to the IRD Stamp Office for stamping within 30 days of execution, and the register of members must be updated within 7 days of lodgment of the transfer. The Annual Return (NAR1) reports registered member particulars and share capital details but does not constitute an annual UBO confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$900 - US$2,500 per annum for a standard Hong Kong registered office, company secretary, and local compliance agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 - US$10,000 per annum for an active private company; the fee increases for consolidated group structures, complex intercompany transactions, or additional transfer pricing reporting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified software enterprises may access the two-year exemption and three-year half-rate tax holiday; key software enterprises may pay 10%; high-technology enterprises may pay 15%; additional R&D deduction of 100% of qualifying anti-cheat engine R&D expenses; certain preferential free-trade zone projects may access 15% reduced CIT under applicable regional legislation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (A-Class Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) together with Schedule A100000 attachments, including the related-party transaction reporting schedules and non-resident withholding supplementary forms, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic e-Taxation / Electronic Taxpayer Filing Portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly interim prepayments. The quarterly prepayment return is due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual final corporate income tax return is due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, with the final tax payment due on the same deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayments must be filed and paid within 15 days of the close of each calendar quarter. The annual CIT final settlement return must be filed within 5 months after fiscal year-end, for example May 31 for a calendar-year taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, jurisdiction of incorporation, enterprise type, ISIC/NAICS industry classification, registration address, and non-resident shareholding details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: As a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture with the Hong Kong investor as ultimate non-resident shareholder, state the precise shareholding percentage, identify whether the Hong Kong shareholder is a resident of Hong Kong SAR for DTA purposes, and confirm the mainland-resident JV is not itself a non-resident enterprise for the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, and separate disclosure of related-party revenue from the Hong Kong parent or affiliated licensees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue from anti-cheat middleware software licenses, maintenance, cloud integration, and kernel-level security services must be recognized under PRC accounting standards; related-party transactions with the Hong Kong affiliate must be reflected in the TP schedules and any adjustment to arm's-length pricing must be carried into Box 2.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, administrative expenses, selling expenses, finance costs, and other deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to the Hong Kong affiliate for software IP, license fees, and technical services must be supported by contracts, withholding tax credentials, and a substance/beneficial-ownership file; expenses that are not supported by BO invoices, with no withholding, or that violate the DTA beneficial-ownership requirement will be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: book profit adjusted by permanent and temporary differences, tax exempt income, non-deductible items, and prior-year tax loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward for 5 years. The Hong Kong investor's losses are not available to the mainland JV. Any transfer pricing adjustment, thin capitalization interest limitation, or denial of royalties will increase taxable income here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable CIT rate, tax base, computed tax liability, reduced/incentive rates, and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory 25% rate unless a software enterprise, high-technology enterprise, or free-trade-zone incentive is qualified. The Hong Kong investor's DTA relief is not taken on this form; rather, it impacts the withholding tax remitted on distributions and cross-border payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, prepaid quarterly CIT, tax payments already made, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset quarterly prepayments against final liability. Any shortfall must be paid before the statutory deadline; any overpayment may be refunded or credited under tax administration rules. The board must ensure no non-resident dividend, interest, or royalty payment is made before required withholding is settled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions schedule: identity of related parties, transaction types, pricing method, intra-group service charges, intangible property transfers, and interest payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all transactions with the Hong Kong affiliate, including anti-cheat software licensing, R&D cost-sharing, technical support, and financing. Select the arm's-length method for each category and prepare the Local File if statutory related-party transaction thresholds are exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding declaration: dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees paid to foreign beneficiaries during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The mainland JV, as withholding agent, must file the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return for each outbound remittance to Hong Kong. Even after claiming a reduced DTA rate, the withholding return must be filed and the tax remitted within 7 days of the payment date; failure to do so triggers withholding-agent liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious cases; late payment attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. An understatement due to false related-party disclosures or fraudulent returns is subject to a penalty of 50% to three times the additional tax, and tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 and 10% of tax payable may constitute a criminal offense under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years and fines for directly responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic statutory withholding tax rate on outbound dividends from the mainland JV to the Hong Kong shareholder is 10%. Under Article 10 of the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement, the dividend WHT is reduced to 5% where the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong company directly holding at least 25% of the paying company's capital; otherwise the treaty rate is 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the reduced 5% dividend rate or 7% interest/royalty rates under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement, the Hong Kong recipient must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the Inland Revenue Department stating that it is a Hong Kong tax resident and that it is the beneficial owner of the income. The mainland JV withholding agent must collect the certificate, a beneficial-ownership self-declaration, the underlying agreements, board resolutions, and evidence of substantive business activity in Hong Kong such as premises, employees, and core income-generating activities. The withholding agent then files the Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return and remits the reduced tax to the State Taxation Administration within 7 days of payment. If the Hong Kong company is a mere shell or conduit, the STA will deny treaty benefits and apply the statutory 10% WHT plus interest and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT for outbound interest and royalties is 10%. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement, approved interest derived by a Hong Kong-resident beneficial owner is limited to 7%, and approved royalties for software, technical know-how, and industrial/commercial/scientific equipment are also limited to 7%. The domestic statutory rates continue to apply unless the full treaty-relief protocol, including Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership substantiation, is completed before remittance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Public Notice [2016] No. 42, a contemporaneous Local File is mandatory for a mainland enterprise where annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, or RMB 40 million for service transactions; a Master File may also be required where the MNE group's related-party transaction scale and consolidated revenue meet the statutory thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although the People's Republic of China does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, the State Taxation Administration applies the OECD's principal-purpose test and the beneficial-ownership doctrine under SAT Public Notice [2018] No. 9. The Hong Kong intermediate holding and IP licensing entity must demonstrate substantive business operations, actual premises, qualified employees, significant decision-making authority, and core income-generating activities in Hong Kong. Substance is required both to claim treaty relief and to validate cross-border charges; a Hong Kong mailbox company or pass-through IP conduit will be disregarded for tax treaty purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and DTA Treaty Shopping Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong shareholder is a nominee or mailbox company with no employees, premises, or real decision-making power in Hong Kong, holds anti-cheat software IP without substance, receives dividends and royalty payments from the mainland JV, and immediately channels the profits onward to a third-country ultimate beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The State Taxation Administration may invoke the General Anti-Abuse Rule under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and SAT Public Notice [2018] No. 9 to deny the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA benefits, reassess the full 10% statutory withholding tax or adjust the mainland JV's deductions, impose a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and impose an additional penalty of 50% to three times the tax understated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil under PRC Company Law Article 20 where the director used the corporate form to abuse limited liability; the director becomes jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and civil restitution. The tax authority may blacklist the director under the major tax violation list, leading to exit restrictions and travel bans under the Exit-Entry Administration Law, and criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 can result in imprisonment of up to 7 years for a major evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Defective Related-Party Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The mainland JV sells anti-cheat middleware software licenses to the Hong Kong affiliate at artificially low prices or pays inflated royalties for IP that has no connection to Hong Kong CIGA; the JV fails to prepare a Local File or Master File despite exceeding the statutory thresholds and does not conduct a comparability analysis or TNMM benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority makes a special tax adjustment under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 41, recharacterizes or reallocates profits, disallows excessive related-party charges, collects additional tax, applies daily interest of 0.05% on the underpayment, and imposes penalties under the Tax Collection Administration Law; failure to file required TP documentation may also attract a separate administrative fine under SAT Public Notice [2016] No. 42.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If directors knowingly sign false related-party agreements, approve fictitious invoices, or cause the preparation of fraudulent TP documents, they may be treated as directly responsible managers under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 and face imprisonment of up to 7 years, fines, civil damages to the corporate treasury, and exit bans or blacklisting as seriously dishonest taxpayers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Withholding Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The board instructs the finance team to omit anti-cheat subscription and licensing revenue, destroy accounting records, file false returns in the name of a dummy entity, fail to withhold 10% WHT on outbound dividends or royalties, and fraudulently claim the DTA reduced rates without a Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial-ownership evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation triggers Criminal Law Article 201 where the evaded tax amount exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax due, with fines and imprisonment up to 7 years; civil and administrative penalties under the Tax Collection Administration Law include recovery of the unpaid tax, a daily surcharge of 0.05%, and a penalty of 50% to three times the evaded tax for the corporate taxpayer, plus additional withholding-agent penalties of 50% to three times the untaxed amount under Article 69.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the director used the company as a fraud device; directors may be jointly and severally liable for restitution of the evaded tax. The tax authority can blacklist directors, impose travel and exit bans, and the criminal court may sentence the responsible director to up to 7 years imprisonment, concurrently with monetary fines and confiscation of the proceeds of tax evasion.
